messages:
sara_support: Heads-up — customer on Dedicated (reserved pool eu-west-1) reporting intermittent 429s during long streaming completions right after autoscale events. They see rapid 429 spikes for long-lived connections and rate-limit headers that look wrong (Remaining: -1, Retry-After: 0). Case attached: CID-4567.

ops-bot: case CID-4567 created and routed to support. Priority: P2.

jane_cse: Repro steps from customer: 1) open streaming chat request that lasts ~45s 2) autoscaler adds capacity (scale up) mid-request 3) subsequent tokens intermittently get 429 and stream cut. They captured headers and a request id: req_0b4f2c.

diego_infra: Can you paste the raw headers/log snippet they captured? also what model variant and reserved pool config?

jane_cse: Snippet they shared:```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-Request-Id: req_0b4f2c
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120
X-RateLimit-Remaining: -1
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1700001234
Retry-After: 0
Content-Type: application/json
```They're on dedicated-pool: eu-west-1, pool size 4, autoscale target 8, burst_window_ms=1000. Model: redwood-2.1-large.

aaron_runtime: Thanks. This looks like token-bucket state mismatch during the worker handoff. Long-lived streaming connections keep a server-side token reservation. When autoscaler creates new workers, our centralized quota cache sometimes synchronizes a negative remaining value for the reserved key. That explains Remaining: -1 and Retry-After: 0 (window already expired but counters went negative).

aaron_runtime: Quick repro I used locally:```bash
# open a long streaming request then trigger a scale up (simulate by adding worker)
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-2.1-large","stream":true,"prompt":"long story"}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream | sed -n '1,200p'
```You should see 429 chunks mid-stream when I flip the pool size.

diego_infra: Can you confirm whether the rate-limit coordination is based on centralized counter or per-worker window? My read of the telemetry earlier was we use central token-bucket but with ephemeral per-worker lease caching. Lease expiry might be too long causing double-spending.

aaron_runtime: Exactly — per-worker cache TTL is 2s in prod. If scale events cause worker reassignments faster than cache refresh, two workers think they own tokens for same key. For streaming, we decrement per-chunk which amplifies the effect. The negative remaining appears when a new worker sees the central state after it already consumed cached tokens.

jane_cse: Customer asks for immediate mitigation. They can't afford client changes. Any temporary server-side knobs we can flip?

diego_infra: Short-term: increase central sync frequency (drop cache ttl to 200ms) or change streaming path not to decrement until chunk commit. Both have cost. I'd prefer a low-risk knob: enable "stream-soft-burst" for that dedicated pool (allow 200 tokens of soft burst per-connection) and set fallback to older model variant during scale.

aaron_runtime: Agreed. Steps: 1) enable stream-soft-burst=200 for reserved pool eu-west-1 (ops change) 2) reduce per-worker cache TTL to 200ms (infra config) 3) add guard in runtime: if X-RateLimit-Remaining < 0, map to Retry-After=50ms instead of 0 to avoid immediate cut.

sara_support: Can someone do 1) and 2) as short-term? Also we need a communication line to customer about temporary mitigations and ETA for full fix.

diego_infra: I'll apply stream-soft-burst in the console for that pool now and open infra change CHG-7789 to lower cache TTL. Expect propagation ~10min for knob, TTL change requires config rollout ~30min.

ops-bot: CHG-7789 created, change window started.

aaron_runtime: I'll draft a runtime patch to avoid negative remaining edge-case (simple clamp) and a longer-term fix: make token allocation atomic via a single-write CAS on central quota store. Patch branch: fix/stream-rate-limit-clamp. PR incoming in a few hours.

jane_cse: I'll update the customer: telling them we applied a soft-burst for their pool and we're rolling a config change; asking them to verify if stream stability improves in next 15-20 minutes. :thumbsup:

sara_support: Thanks. Please mark this thread when you have verification. After we confirm, we should schedule a postmortem to discuss telemetry gaps and add a canary for scaling events affecting streaming requests. :eyes:

diego_infra: Verified soft-burst applied, logs show fewer 429s for req_0b4f2c after change. Keeping monitoring window open 1h.

aaron_runtime: PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/452 — implements clamp and adds unit test for streaming decrement race. Will coordinate canary deploy after CHG-7789 completes.

sara_support: Great — leaving this on our radar. Closing temporary escalation when customer confirms.

ops-bot: case CID-4567 updated: mitigation applied, awaiting customer confirmation.
